text:
Where is the memory of the days
+        that were yours on earth, and wove
+        happiness and pain and were the universe to you?
+
+
+        The numerable river of the years
+        has lost them; you are a word in an index.
+
+
+        The gods gave others endless glory,
+        inscriptions and exergues and monuments and punctual historians;
+        of you we know only, obscure friend,
+        that you heard the nightingale one afternoon.
+
+
+        Among the asphodels of shadow, your vain shade
+        will think the gods have been miserly.
+
+
+        But days are a net of trivial miseries,
+        and what better fortune could there be than to be the ash
+        of which oblivion is made?
+
+
+        Upon others the gods cast
+        the inexorable light of glory, which looks into the entrails and counts the cracks,
+        of glory, which ends by tarnishing the rose it venerates;
+        with you they were more merciful, brother.
+
+
+        In the ecstasy of an evening that will not become night,
+        you hear the voice of Theocritus’s nightingale.

translation.title: To a Minor Poet in the Anthology
translation.editorial_note: This titled witness uses the same reviewed diction as the first-line version, while preserving the indented anthology layout.
